## Parties

This Mutual Confidentiality Agreement is entered into by and between Ironbridge Data SARL (the "First Party") and Dunmore Slate Ltd (the "Second Party"), each referred to individually as a "Party" and together as the "Parties". This Agreement takes effect on 13 June 2026 (the "Effective Date") and is entered into in connection with an integration of two products (the "Purpose").

## Confidential Information

"Confidential Information" means any information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party"), whether before or after the Effective Date, in writing, orally, electronically, visually or by any other means, and whether or not marked or identified as confidential, that relates to the Purpose or to the Disclosing Party's business, products, technology or affairs. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, technical data, product designs, architecture and specifications, source code, application programming interfaces and interface documentation, integration plans and test results, roadmaps, business plans, pricing, customer and supplier information, financial information, and the existence and contents of this Agreement and of the discussions between the Parties concerning the Purpose.

Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party; (b) was lawfully in the Receiving Party's possession, free of any obligation of confidence, before disclosure by the Disclosing Party; (c) is lawfully received from a third party who is under no obligation of confidence in respect of it; or (d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Confidential Information.

## Obligations

Each Receiving Party shall hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence and shall use it solely for the Purpose and for no other purpose. The Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party, except to its employees, officers, directors, professional advisers and contractors who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those set out in this Agreement; the Receiving Party remains responsible for any breach by such persons. The Receiving Party shall apply at least the same degree of care to the Confidential Information as it applies to its own confidential information of similar importance, and in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. The Receiving Party shall not copy, decompile or reverse engineer the Confidential Information except as reasonably required for the Purpose, and shall promptly notify the Disclosing Party upon becoming aware of any unauthorised use or disclosure. Disclosure compelled by law, regulation or a competent authority is permitted, provided the Receiving Party gives the Disclosing Party prompt written notice where lawful to do so and discloses only the portion legally required. Upon written request, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy the Confidential Information in its possession, subject to retention required by law or routine backup.

## Term

This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a term of 60 months.

## Governing Law

This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by and construed in accordance with the law of France.
